title: Level 3 (Advanced) - B-10
notes:
West leads the ♥K against 4♠. West's heart opening lead is overtaken by East. East cashes a second round of hearts and continues a third round. South ruffs and West overruffs. West returns a diamond, South winning.

South should draw trump noting that East started with 3 spades. South must somehow avoid the loss of a club trick. There are 2 possible ways this might be accomplished. If East has the doubleton ♣QJ, they will drop under the ♣A and ♣K making the ♣10 high.

If East has a singleton ♣J or ♣Q, South can cash the ♣A dropping East's honour. A finessing position now exists over West's club honour.

Before playing a second round of clubs, South should probe the diamond distribution by cashing 2 more rounds of that suit. When East follows to both rounds of diamonds, he is counted for 3 spades, 6 hearts, 3 diamonds, and therefore a singleton club. South will be able to finesse the ♣10 with complete confidence.

If East discards on the third round of diamonds, he must have 2 clubs. His distribution is 3 spades, 6 hearts, 2 diamonds, and 2 clubs. South will know to cash the ♣K on the second round, hoping East was dealt the doubleton ♣QJ.
